classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the scatterplot representing perfect negative correlation.

content.prompt:
For a set of bivariate data, Pearson's correlation coefficient is $-1$.

Which graph could best represent this set of bivariate data?

spec.description: Four horizontally arranged options A–D, with arrowed x and y axes extending slightly beyond their intersection. No ticks or numerical scales.
spec.mathematics: A: four non-collinear rising points. B: four descending points, with the last two vertically aligned. C: four exactly collinear rising points. D: four exactly collinear falling points.
spec.answerVisibility: All four options are permanent student-visible givens; the correct option is not marked.

answer.worked: $r=-1$ represents perfect negative correlation: all points lie on a straight line falling from left to right. Graph D has this pattern. Correct answer: D.
